newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus dismisses German comments on EU membership.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus dismisses German comments on EU membership.

text.p: Cyprus on Tuesday shrugged off scepticism expressed by German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel about the island's chances of joining the EU as long as it remained divided.

In a pointed rebuff to the German minister, Cypriot government spokesman Yiannakis Cassoulides said Kinkel's comments did not concur with those of the European Union, which is due to open accession negotiations with the island in the next year.
"We will continue our course to the EU because it is not Germany we want to be a member of but the European Union," Cassoulides said.
Kinkel said in Brussels on Monday that Cyprus, whose Turkish and Greek Cypriot communities have lived apart since 1974, could not become a member until the long-standing dispute was settled.
"Anyone who wants to join the EU must know that the European Union cannot deal with the accession of new members that bring in additional external problems," he told reporters.
But Cassoulides said: "Mr Kinkel should remember if there was one country which had significant problems in Europe it was his, which suffered the consequences of partition for years."
Germany's reunification may not have been a political headache for the EU, but it brought financial problems, he said.
Turkey has occupied northern Cyprus since 1974 when its troops invaded in response to a short-lived Greek Cypriot coup in the capital Nicosia.
